Content:

- The global minimum of a function is the smallest [MATH: y]-value that the function attains on its domain. There can only be (at most) one global minimum. It's also called the absolute minimum.

If one or both exist, the global maximum and minimum values of a function are collectively called the global extrema of the function.

sections.normalized_html:
First, we recall the following definitions:

  • The global maximum of a function is the largest value that the function attains on its domain. There can only be (at most) one global maximum.

  • A global maximum point is a point [MATH: (x,y)] where a function reaches a global maximum. There can be zero, one, or many global maximum points.

For our function, the maximum value reached by the function is [MATH: f(x)=4.] Therefore, the global maximum is [MATH: 4.] The function reaches this value when [MATH: x=-1,] so the global maximum point is [MATH: (-1,4).]

items.title: Identifying Whether the Global Extrema of a Function Exist

sections.normalized_html:
The graph [MATH: y = f(x)] is shown below. Which of the following statements is true?

  1. The global maximum of [MATH: f(x)] is [MATH: 1.]

  2. The global minimum of [MATH: f(x)] is [MATH: -4.]

  3. The function does not have any global extrema.
sections.readable_text:
The graph [MATH: y = f(x)] is shown below. Which of the following statements is true?

1. The global maximum of [MATH: f(x)] is [MATH: 1.]
2. The global minimum of [MATH: f(x)] is [MATH: -4.]
3. The function does not have any global extrema.

[IMG: /graphics/0109191806104381c345a7fd6e1a07f5]

sections.normalized_html:
Let's examine each statement.

  • Statement I is false. As [MATH: x] increases on the right-hand side of the graph, the function continues to increase without bound (as indicated by the arrow). So, the function does not reach a global maximum value.

  • Statement II is false. At first glance, it might seem that the point [MATH: (-4,-4)] corresponds to the global minimum, but since [MATH: x=-4] is not included in the domain (as indicated by the open circle), the function does not have a global minimum.

  • Statement III is true. The function does not have a global maximum and does not have a global minimum. Therefore, the function does not have any global extrema.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
